name: Giorgio de Chirico

src.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
src.q: Beginning in 1900, de Chirico studied drawing and painting at Athens Polytechnic—mainly under the guidance of the Greek painters Georgios Roilos and Georgios Jakobides.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
notes.q: De Chirico found inspiration in the unexpected sensations that familiar places or things sometimes produced in him: In a manuscript of 1909, he wrote of the "host of strange, unknown and solitary things that can be translated into painting ...

src.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
src.q: De Chirico returned to Italy in the summer of 1909 and spent six months in Milan.

src.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
src.q: At the beginning of 1910, he moved to Florence, where he painted the first of his 'Metaphysical Town Square' series, The Enigma of an Autumn Afternoon, after the revelation he felt in Piazza Santa Croce.

notes.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
notes.q: During 1913, he exhibited paintings at the Salon des Indépendants and Salon d'Automne; his work was noticed by Pablo Picasso and Guillaume Apollinaire, and he sold his first painting, The Red Tower.

src.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
src.q: In July 1911, he spent a few days in Turin on his way to Paris.

src.name: Wikipedia · Giorgio de Chirico
src.q: De Chirico met and married his first wife, the Russian ballerina Raissa Gurievich (1894–1979) in 1925, and together they moved to Paris.
